name: Xinja
one_liner: App-only Australian challenger bank that won a full banking licence then handed it back
story: Xinja built an app-only neobank and won a full Australian banking licence, attracting 37,884 customers with more than A$252M in deposits. A promised A$433M investment from Dubai-based World Investments was paused, and with COVID-19 hitting capital markets it could not raise enough to keep operating. In December 2020 it returned 99.97% of deposits (the rest moved to NAB) and APRA revoked its licence.

name: Volt Bank
one_liner: Australian digital-only bank that shut after failing to raise a A$200M Series F
story: Volt was an Australian digital-only bank that raised almost A$85M in 2021 (about US$64M at 0.75) and went back to market in early 2022 for a A$200M Series F. When that raise failed, the board closed the business in June 2022 and handed back its banking licence, with about A$113M of deposits from some 6,000 customers returned or moved to NAB.
